quotes.text: Record if [Name] is person in whose name this accommodation is owned or rented
You told me that [NumHhldrs] people jointly own or rent the accommodation. Which of you/them has the highest income (from earnings, benefits, pensions and any other sources)?
Enter person number of the eldest (joint householder) from those listed below
Enter PerNo of person providing information about this respondent
From spring 2001 the LFS is switching from using Head of Household (HOH) to Household Reference Person (HRP) in line with all other ONS household surveys.
The HRP will take into account accommodation ownership / rental, income and age in order to identify the HRP

assessments.reasoning:
The supplied documents establish the following regarding the four elements:
1. neutral_anchor_term: True. The instrument uses 'Household Reference Person' (HRP) rather than 'head of household' as the primary category for identifying the anchor person.
2. explicit_selection_rule: True. An explicit rule is stated: the HRP is the person in whose name the accommodation is owned or rented (HRPID), and in cases of joint ownership/tenancy, the person with the highest income (HIHNUM), or if equal/refused, the eldest joint householder (JNTELDA/JNTELDB).
3. rule_not_sex_age_authority: False. The stated selection criteria explicitly invoke highest income ('highest income') and seniority ('eldest') as tie-breakers among joint householders.
4. respondent_separate_or_any_adult: True. The questionnaire explicitly records the person providing information for each respondent via RESPNO ('Enter PerNo of person providing information about this respondent').
